post.contentHtml:
Revenue Surges, Profit Grows Only in Single Digits: The Disconnect at Zigexn

Zigexn (じげん, 3679) is a "life media platform" company that gathers information on everyday needs such as job hunting and career changes, nurse recruitment, real estate, and used cars in one place. It is listed on the Prime Market of the Tokyo Stock Exchange. Based on the interim results announced on November 12, this article looks at the gap between revenue growth and the share price.

The share price data is the November 13 closing price of 446 yen. I could not confirm the closing price for the 18th, so please treat it as a reference. This price is about 9.7% lower than a year ago.

What the interim results confirmed

  • After the market closed on November 12, the company released its results for the first half (April–September) of the fiscal year ending March 2027. The accounting standard is International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS).
  • First-half net profit rose 7.2% year on year to about 2.12 billion yen. Looking at the July–September quarter alone, it increased by about 5%.
  • Progress against the full-year plan is 48.4%, almost the same as the five-year average (48.7%). This means things are on track with the plan, not that they have exceeded expectations.
  • First-quarter (April–June) revenue, announced earlier, was about 7.8 billion yen, up 15.5% year on year. For a first quarter, revenue and profit at every level were the highest ever.

In what I was able to check, there was no mention of the full-year plan being raised. However, I did not review the original earnings release, so whether any revision was made should be confirmed again through the company's disclosures.

Why is there a "disconnect"?

When revenue grows by double digits but profit grows by only single digits, it means profit is not keeping pace with the growth in revenue. Zigexn has expanded its business through mergers and acquisitions (M&A), so even when acquisitions lift revenue, costs and amortization (the gradual write-off of acquisition-related assets) can rise along with it. That said, the specific reason for this profit slowdown is my own estimate, not something confirmed in the company's disclosures.

There was also an assessment that first-quarter profit fell short of the market consensus (the average forecast of brokerage analysts). If the market expects high growth but profit growth stays in the 5–7% range, it is hard for the share price to rise.

Where it stands in numbers

ItemDetails
Recent share price (11/13)446 yen
1-year share price changeabout -9.7%
Expected dividend for FY ending March 2027about 13.5 yen per share (about 3% of the recent share price)
Brokerage target price1 firm counted, 700 yen (for reference)

The dividend yield is a simple calculation: the expected dividend divided by the recent share price. The target price is the opinion of just one firm, so its reliability is low.

Notable points in the shareholder structure

  • KK Jogen is the largest shareholder with about 44.5%. Judging by the name, it may be an entity related to the founder, but this is an estimate.
  • Fidelity Management & Research holds about 5.7%, and Fidelity Institutional Asset Management holds about 2.9%.
  • Others include Hirao (Jo) at about 4.8% and Nomura Trust and Banking at about 2.9%.

When the largest shareholder holds a large stake, the number of shares actually traded in the market can be small. The median annual trading value is about 118 million yen, which is not large. Because trading is thin, you should keep in mind that the share price can swing sharply.

What to watch next

  • Profit growth rate: We need to see in the second-half quarterly results whether revenue growth translates into profit growth.
  • Achieving the full-year plan: Since progress is at the five-year average, the question is whether there is room to beat the plan in the second half.
  • M&A effects: The key is whether the acquired businesses contribute to better profitability.
  • Dividend policy: The expected dividend is higher than before, so it is worth watching whether it is maintained.

In summary, Zigexn's business does not appear to be collapsing; rather, there seems to be a gap between its growth pace and market expectations. Whether this gap narrows is likely to determine the direction of the share price going forward.
